chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Reuben's place and the cutting contests
summary: The Harlem pianists held cutting contests at Reuben's on 130th Street, attended by Fats, the Lion, Basie, Tatum and Donald Lambert.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: So we'd all go down to a fellow's place named Reuben on 130th Street between Seventh and Eighth. Reuben had a place, he owned the building. So he built the thing downstairs for the fellows (but he served nothing) (but beer and wine) that old, funny kind of whiskey. But that's where Art Tatum (unintelligible) used to go.
What was the name of the place?
This was Rueben, yeah. I see his brother once in a while now by 130th Street.
Did he have a good piano?
No, he had a good piano because Fats the Lion and Basie and Art Tatum and this guy from over New -- named Donald Lambert -- see, he was a most underrated piano player. People never realized.
Well, I've heard some of those things he did, and he sure is good.
